postOneTitle: 15 minutes of shadowing a day: what changed?
postOneBody: I used to catch individual words but lose the rest of the sentence. This week I tried a short clip: listen, read the transcript, then repeat it three times. Matching the rhythm before the speed has made speaking feel much easier. What helps you keep a daily habit?
postTwoTitle: A little notebook for easily confused words 🌱
postTwoBody: Instead of writing each word ten times, I put two similar words side by side and write one personal example. Today: 聞く and 聴く. Then I schedule a review for tomorrow. A page a day is plenty, as long as I understand the sentences I write.
postThreeTitle: Looking for a weekend N4 study partner
postThreeBody: I am reviewing N4 grammar and listening and would love a weekly study buddy. We could choose a short lesson, each summarize it in three sentences, then discuss the confusing parts. A slow start is fine; consistency matters more.
postFourTitle: Simple phrases I want to try in Kyoto
postFourBody: すみません、ここまで歩いて行けますか。— Excuse me, can I walk here? I like learning whole phrases before a trip because they are easier to recall than isolated words. Which phrase helped you feel more confident while traveling?
